checked: Numerator/top, denominator/bottom, decimal places, percent, terminating decimal, base, part, rate, reciprocal, dividend, divisor, and approximation symbol receive local meanings before the examples need them.
Decimal-to-fraction teaching connects denominator to place value and reduction. Common denominators make equal-sized parts; multiplication finds a fraction of an amount.
Reciprocal division is justified by making the divisor 1. Equal shifts preserve a quotient. Percentage base selection is explained through the reference amount and successive prices.
Core excludes zero fraction denominators and zero divisors, restricts the direct decimal-place method to terminating decimals, and states nonzero rate/base conditions for division.
Later discounts use new bases; percent more adds the increase; approximate thirds are marked as rounded. These cover the limitations of the methods used.
